macro.headline: Bull regime intact but momentum cooling under dollar squeeze
macro.story:
The market is in a transitional posture. SPY and QQQ both sit above their 50- and 200-day moving averages with the broader Russell 2000 and Dow joining the uptrend, yet the daily momentum picture has rolled over: MACD on SPY, QQQ, and Nasdaq has slipped below signal even as prices remain elevated. VIX has fallen to 17 (down 12% in five days) and the term structure is in healthy contango, so this is not a fear environment — it is a momentum digestion inside a bull regime, with SPY just 0.5% off its 52-week high.

The dominant cross-asset catalyst grounded in the active themes is the AI Infrastructure capex cycle (CHASING stage, conviction 8) compounded by the Geopolitical Risk Unwind (Iran deal / Hormuz reopening). Capital is being funded by hedge unwinds: gold is down ~8% over 21 days, silver down ~14%, and WTI crude is down 22% over the same window with RSI at 31 — classic risk-premium liquidation. The dollar (DXY) is the swing factor, with RSI at 70 and extended above its Bollinger upper band; that strength is the validated headwind pressing on gold and silver right now.

Under the surface, leadership is rotating away from defensives and into cyclicals and small-caps. Financials, Industrials, Materials, and the Russell 2000 all sit in HOT heat states with bullish MACD, while Energy and Communication Services have collapsed to weak readings (Energy RSI 34, Comm Services RSI 33). The yield curve has flattened sharply — the 10y-2y spread is down 48% in 21 days as the 2y yield pushes overbought — signaling the bond market is repricing a higher-for-longer front end, which is consistent with the dollar bid.

Net read for a long-only trader: the validated Early-Runway rotation tailwind is alive in cyclicals (Travel, Resorts, Computer Hardware, Capital Markets), so this is a stockpicker's tape. But macro confidence is capped at MEDIUM because daily momentum has rolled over even with price extended, and the dollar squeeze plus oil washout argue for selectivity, not aggression.
